comments: All 9 acceptance criteria approved. Recorded on the reviewer's instruction given in chat and transcribed by the orchestrator; the decision is the reviewer's, the transcription is not an agent approval. Approving this artifact also confirms the resolutions of AMB-ETA-411-001 through AMB-ETA-411-005, which the reviewer answered on 2026-09-01 and which are recorded in the source artifact with resolvedBy. Three consequences carry forward and must not be quietly forgotten downstream. (1) AMB-ETA-411-002 was resolved as 'the landing URL is acceptable proof'. A URL assertion cannot distinguish a correctly rendered page from one that reached the right address but rendered an error, an empty result or a permission refusal; such a case will pass. This is an accepted risk, not an oversight. (2) AMB-ETA-411-003 was answered as 'the icon set is identical for all organization users'. That is the reviewer's assertion about intended behaviour, not an observation - reconnaissance used a single account. The overlapping AMB-ETA-351-006 remains open for ETA-351 and is not closed by this approval. (3) AMB-ETA-411-005 was resolved as 'accept the Command Center control as-is'. The control still exposes no accessible name, so keyboard and assistive-technology users have no named control to operate; AC-ETA-411-006 will pass regardless, and the gap is deliberately left unfiled as a defect. AMB-ETA-411-006 was NOT answered at this gate and remains REVIEW_REQUIRED: the header exposes no Preferences link, so New Transaction and Workspace each have two routes while Preferences has one, and whether the menu link labelled 'Organization' counts as a third route is undecided. Test plan scope must reflect that asymmetry as it stands and must not invent a header Preferences route. AC-ETA-411-008 and AC-ETA-411-009 are approved on href evidence only - neither header link was ever activated during reconnaissance - so PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION must confirm both destinations by navigation before any test asserts them.

itemDecisions.comment: Organization user who signs in arrives at the Home page. Observed.

Home page offers three activatable dashboard tiles: New Transaction, Workspace, Preferences. Observed, not stated in Jira. Holds as a product statement only on the strength of the AMB-ETA-411-003 answer, since a single account was observed.

New Transaction tile leads to the New Transaction page. Destination observed by navigation. Proven by landing URL; a unique 'Create Transaction' heading is available as a stronger secondary check if wanted.
Workspace tile leads to the Workspace page. Destination observed by navigation. Landing URL is the only discriminator; this destination exposes no unique on-screen element.
Preferences tile leads to the Preferences page. Destination observed by navigation. Landing URL is the only discriminator; this destination exposes no unique on-screen element.

Command Center control in the upper left returns the user Home. Observed by navigation on all three return legs. Automation may use the #bannerBackground id selector with a VALIDATED waiver; the absent accessible name is knowingly accepted and not filed.
Header navigation offers New Transaction and Workspace links duplicating the tiles. Deliberately TWO links, not three: no header Preferences link exists. Do not add one. See AMB-ETA-411-006.

Header New Transaction link leads to the New Transaction page. Approved on href evidence only; the link was never activated. PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION must walk it before any test asserts the destination.
Header Workspace link leads to the Workspace page. Approved on href evidence only; the link was never activated. PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION must walk it before any test asserts the destination.
